ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the diagram of the food web shown, what is a consumer of the large shark?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The food web diagram shows sunlight at the top, then one-celled life, shrimplike creatures, small fish, mackerel, tuna, and a large shark. Arrows point from one-celled life to shrimplike creatures, from shrimplike creatures to small fish, from small fish toward mackerel, from mackerel down toward tuna, and from tuna toward the large shark. Reasoning: The arrows indicate food/energy moving from the organism being eaten to the organism that consumes it. Since the arrow from tuna points to the large shark, the large shark consumes tuna. To find a consumer of the large shark, there would need to be an arrow starting at the large shark and pointing to another organism. The diagram shows no arrow leaving the large shark, so no organism is shown consuming it.
